A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 31-page theoretical work. Pages 2–31 are textually and visually identical; only the first-page title and arXiv version/date stamp differ. Neither PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms and mathematical proofs, without original empirical outcomes. Section 2's graph examples and Section 4's numerical bounds are analytical results.

after.justification: v3 retains the same theoretical content and adds no experiments, simulations, user studies, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: ModifiedPivot in Algorithm 1 and its dynamic maintenance procedure in Section 5 are identical, including sampling, vertex reassignment, and update rules.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or empirical tasks. The theoretical correlation-clustering setting and illustrative graph families are unchanged.

E2.justification: The analytical comparisons with Pivot and discussion of prior approximation algorithms are identical. Neither version reports empirical baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental evaluation protocols, training budgets, data splits, or empirical metrics.

E4.justification: The illustrative failure examples in Section 2 and subsequent case analyses are identical. No empirical ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary studies are added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The unchanged expectations and probability bounds are theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: All numerical bounds and example costs are unchanged, including Theorem 2's 2.997 approximation factor. Neither version contains empirical result entries.

T1.justification: The definitions, charging scheme, lemmas, and proofs in Sections 3–5 are identical, including both the approximation guarantee and the dynamic update-time analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contribution: modifying Pivot to obtain an approximation below 3 with polylogarithmic expected update time. The new title does not alter these substantive claims.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and qualifications are unchanged. Remark 4.1 still states that the approximation constant was not optimized, and Theorem 1 retains its oblivious-adversary and expectation qualifications.

D1.justification: Algorithm parameters, the numerical parameter choices in the proof of Lemma 4.5, and Section 5's data structures and implementation details are identical. No code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: The same 22 references and discussion of prior work are retained. Positioning relative to Pivot and earlier dynamic correlation-clustering algorithms is unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Fully Dynamic Correlation Clustering: Breaking 3-Approximation' to 'Correlation Clustering Beyond the Pivot Algorithm,' and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining prose and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: Graph illustrations, algorithm boxes, mathematical displays, and page organization are unchanged. The revised title and version/date text occupy the existing first-page layout.

improvement.justification: The revision changes only the title and arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific content, proofs, implementation discussion, and substantive presentation are identical, so these editorial changes do not materially improve or weaken the paper.
